hints.title: Maximal Product Partition Obstacle
hints.text: Breaking integer n into at least two positive integers to maximize their product requires balancing sub-factor products. How can splitting into sub-factor i - j versus further breaking i - j compose the largest product?

hints.title: Subproblem Product Maximization Invariant
hints.text: For any partition choice j, the product is j multiplied by the maximum between remaining value i - j and the optimal broken product of i - j.

hints.title: 1D Array Bottom-Up Maximization Procedure
hints.text: Initialize an array of size n + 1 with base case 1 at index 1. For each i from 2 to n, check all split candidates j from 1 to i // 2, updating entry i to be the maximum of its existing value, j * (i - j), and j * entry[i - j]. Return entry n.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Nested loops compute max product for each number up to N.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all integer partitions takes exponential Catalan-like time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Array of size N + 1 uses minimal memory for N <= 58.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Considering both breaking and not breaking the remaining subproblem (j * (i - j) vs j * dp[i - j]).
